[[File:RSNZ honours Auckland 2024 3682996 (cropped Gaven Martin).jpg|thumb|Martin in 2024]]
'''Gaven John Martin''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|CNZM|size=85%}} (born 8 October 1958)<ref>[http://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/nr95030236.html Date of birth from Library of Congress authority control data]. Retrieved 20 January 2015.</ref> is a New Zealand mathematician.<ref name="star">{{citation|title=Star of the west: a former "Westie" who grew up reading comics and hot-wiring cars, Gaven Martin is one of the finest mathematicians New Zealand has produced|first=Donna|last=Chisholm|journal=North & South|date=June 2010|url=https://www.math.auckland.ac.nz/mathwiki/images/c/cf/Gaven_Martin_North_and_South_June_2010.pdf|pages=83–87}}</ref><ref name="nzms">{{citation|title=Gaven Martin|department=Centrefold|journal=Newsletter of the New Zealand Mathematical Society|volume=82|date=August 2011|url=https://nzmathsoc.org.nz/downloads/profiles/NZMSprofile82_Gaven_Martin.pdf?t=1263005400}}.</ref> He is a distinguished professor of Mathematics at [[Massey University]], the head of the New Zealand Institute for Advanced Study,<ref name="cv">[http://www.nzias.ac.nz/docs/gavenmartin/gavenmartin_cv.pdf Curriculum vitae]. Retrieved 20 January 2015.</ref> the former president of the [[New Zealand Mathematical Society]] (from 2005 to 2007),<ref>[http://nzmathsoc.org.nz/?historylists Presidents of the NZMS]. Retrieved 22 January 2015.</ref> and former editor-in-chief of the ''New Zealand Journal of Mathematics''.<ref>[http://nzjm.math.auckland.ac.nz/index.php/New_Zealand_Journal_of_Mathematics ''New Zealand Journal of Mathematics'' home page] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150124091946/http://nzjm.math.auckland.ac.nz/index.php/New_Zealand_Journal_of_Mathematics |date=24 January 2015 }}. Retrieved 22 January 2015.</ref> He is a former vice-president of the Royal Society of New Zealand. His research concerns [[quasiconformal mapping]]s, regularity theory for [[partial differential equation]]s, and connections between the theory of [[discrete group]]s and [[low-dimensional topology]].<ref name="nzms"/>

==Education and career==
Martin is originally from [[Rotorua]], New Zealand.<ref name="nzms"/> His family moved to [[Henderson, New Zealand|Henderson]] when he was 11 years old, and he attended [[Henderson High School (Auckland)|Henderson High School]]<ref name="star"/> and the [[University of Auckland]] (as the first of his extended family to go to university), earning a BSc with first-class honours in 1980 and an MSc with distinction in 1981.<ref name="star"/> He then went to the [[University of Michigan]] on a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright scholarship]],<ref name="star"/> completing his doctorate in 1985 under the supervision of [[Frederick Gehring]]<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=7311}}</ref> and earning the [[Sumner Byron Myers]] Prize for the best mathematics dissertation in his year<ref name="star"/> and an A.P. Sloan Foundation Fellowship spent in T.U.B. Berlin and The University of Helsinki.

After short-term positions at the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] of the [[University of California, Berkeley]] and as a Gibbs Instructor at [[Yale University]], Martin became a lecturer at the University of Auckland in 1989,<ref name="cv"/> but left after a year to research at the [[Mittag-Leffler Institute]] in Sweden and the [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques]] in France.<ref name="nzms"/>
Soon after his return, he was given a personal chair at Auckland;<ref name="nzms"/><ref name="cv"/> when he took it, he became (at age 32) the youngest full professor in New Zealand.<ref name="star"/><ref name="nzms"/>
For the next several years, he split his time between Auckland and [[Australian National University]],<ref name="nzms"/><ref name="cv"/> but by 1996, he gave up the Australian appointment and remained solely at Auckland.<ref name="cv"/> He moved to Massey as a distinguished professor in 2005,<ref name="cv"/> and in 2016–2020 served as elected as the academic staff representative on the Massey University Council, the University's topmost governing body.<ref>[http://www.massey.ac.nz/massey/about-massey/university-management/university-council/council_home.cfm Massey University Council]</ref> He currently is the Director of the NZ Mathematics Research Institute https://www.nzmri.org and a long serving board member of the Rotary Science Trust.

==Honours and awards==
Martin became a fellow of the [[Royal Society of New Zealand]] in 1997.<ref name="cv"/> In 2001, he won the James Cook Fellowship of the RSNZ;<ref name="nzms"/><ref name="cv"/> he also won the [[Hector Memorial Medal]] of the RSNZ in 2008.<ref>[http://www.royalsociety.org.nz/programmes/awards/hector-medal/recipients/ Hector Medal recipients], [[Royal Society of New Zealand]]. Retrieved 20 January 2015.</ref> He was an invited speaker at the 2010 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]].<ref name="star"/>
In 2012, he became one of the inaugural [[fellow]]s of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society]. Retrieved 18 January 2015.</ref> He was made a Foreign Member of the Finnish Academy of Science and Letters in 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.massey.ac.nz/massey/about-massey/news/article.cfm?mnarticle_uuid=271F45B9-DECB-15B8-4667-DDCCA8939A07|title=Mathematician's links to Finland honoured|date=27 April 2016|publisher=Massey University}}</ref> 
He gave the Taft Memorial Lectures in 2010<ref>{{cite web |title=Taft Lecture poster |url=https://www.artsci.uc.edu/content/dam/refresh/artsandsciences-62/departments/math/news-and-events/department-lectures/taft-lecture/taft-lectures/martin.pdf |website=University of Cincinnati, College of Arts and Sciences |publisher=University of Cincinnati |access-date=1 January 2025 |date=2006}}</ref> and the Maclaurin Lectures of the American Mathematical Society in 2016.<ref>{{cite web |title=AMS-NZMS Maclaurin Lectureship |url=https://www.ams.org/meetings/lectures/maclaurin-lectures |publisher=American Mathematical Society |access-date=1 January 2025}}</ref> He is a Fellow of the [[New Zealand Mathematical Society]], won their Research Prize (1994) and the inaugural Kalman Prize (2016).<ref>{{cite web |title=NZMS Awards and prizes |url=https://nzmathsoc.org.nz/?awards |publisher=New Zealand Mathematical Society |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240811053742/https://nzmathsoc.org.nz/?awards |access-date=1 January 2025|archive-date=11 August 2024 }}</ref> Recent awards include Japanese Society for the Promotion of Science Fellowships and the Humbolt Research Prize (2022). In 2024, Martin was awarded the Jones Medal by the Royal Society of New Zealand for "his groundbreaking work in a broad range of fields including geometry, analysis, topology, and group theory".<ref>{{cite web |title=2024 Research Honours Aotearoa event in Tāmaki Makaurau Auckland |url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/news/2024-research-honours-aotearoa-event-in-tamaki-makaurau-auckland/ |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand Te Apārangi |access-date=23 November 2024}}</ref>

[[File:Gaven Martin CNZM investiture.jpg|thumb|right|Martin (right), after his investiture as a [[Companion of the New Zealand Order of Merit]] by the governor-general, [[Cindy Kiro|Dame Cindy Kiro]], at [[Government House, Auckland]], on 10 April 2026]]
In the [[2026 New Year Honours (New Zealand)|2026 New Year Honours]], Martin was appointed a [[Companion of the New Zealand Order of Merit]], for services to mathematics and education.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/new-year-2026-honours-the-full-list-of-knights-dames-honourees/J7UOYYMDTRCSXA22HSKNXJGR7Y/ |title=New Year 2026 Honours: The full list of knights, dames, honourees |date=31 December 2025 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |access-date=31 December 2025}}</ref>

==Mathematics education==
In 2021 Martin chaired the Royal Society of New Zealand's Expert Advice Panel for the Ministry of Education  on the NZ Mathematics and Statistics Curriculum.  Their report found that investment and changes were needed at virtually all levels of the education system.<ref>{{cite web |title=pangarau-mathematics-and-tauanga-statistics-in-aotearoa-new-zealand|url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/what-we-do/our-expert-advice/all-expert-advice-papers/pangarau-mathematics-and-tauanga-statistics-in-aotearoa-new-zealand/|access-date=23 November 2021}}</ref>  He was subsequently appointed to the Ministerial Advisory Group <ref>{{cite web |title= AGG named|date=19 December 2023 |url=https://insidegovernment.co.nz/new-education-ministerial-advisory-group-named/}}</ref>
